_comment: Pronunciation lexicon for Video J (narration skill, PRONUNCIATION.md). Only respell and accept change narration; say/ipa/lang/sources/decoy/note/probe are the record. Looked up with lookup_pronunciation.py (two of its guesses, for Moler and Van Loan, were wrong and are replaced by hand, as each note says) and probed with probe_names.py run --write in this video's voice, michael. The script speaks Moler and Van Loan (13_1), Padé (13_5) and Lie (15_4), and the terms commutator, communicability and eigenvalue; Euler, Baker, Campbell, Hausdorff and Estrada are on screen only and are probed because the order lists them. Not in this file because the video only shows them: Bernoulli, Laguerre, Peano, Hatano, Higham, Al-Mohy. Single letters (e, i, t, k, J, A, B) are not lexicon entries: sentences are worded so that a letter never opens one as 'A', and the letter-heavy lines are checked by transcription (docs/claims.md, 'letters'). Re-probe when the voice or the ftts version changes; the owner's pronunciation overrides every entry.

Euler.note: English usage; Wikipedia's lead notes that 'YOO-ler' is considered incorrect. On screen only in this script (who-and-when strips at 05 and 06).

Lie.note: Sophus Lie, Norwegian [liː]: 'Lee'. Spoken at 15_4 ('Lie algebra', 'Lie group'). The ordinary spelling is not offered to the voice: it is the English word 'lie'.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy
probe.verdict: VERIFIED by transcript and spectrogram: 'Lee' heard as Lee 3/3; the plain spelling and the decoy 'Lye' heard as lie/lye/Lai. The probe tool marked it UNVERIFIED only because the decoy's 'lie' is the name's own spelling. Spectrograms of 'This is Lee.' against 'This is Lye.' and 'This is Lie.': Lee ends on a second formant rising into a steady high band (/iː/); both others show the crossing formants of /aɪ/.

Baker.note: Ordinary English. On screen only (the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff strip at 14_6).

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy
probe.verdict: UNVERIFIED, not spoken: the ASR writes Campbell for every read, the decoy too. On screen only (14_6).

Hausdorff.note: English usage as Wikipedia's lead gives it. On screen only (14_6).

Estrada.note: Ernesto Estrada is Cuban-Spanish; the Spanish reading with an English-friendly spelling. Nothing specific to him was found (research notes, item 11). On screen only (11_6).

Moler.note: Cleve Moler, American. The lookup tool matched the Spanish verb 'moler', which is wrong here and was discarded. No written source for his own pronunciation was found; MOH-ler is the conventional reading in numerical analysis talks. Spoken at 13_1: ask the owner if he knows better.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy
probe.verdict: PARTIAL, needs an ear: 'Mohler' heard as 'Mola' 3/3, which is MOH-luh in this non-rhotic voice; the decoy MOLL-er heard as 'mole', 'Moller', 'Moller'; the plain spelling was unstable (Muller, Mollis, Mola) and the hyphenated MOH-ler splits into two chunks. The spectrogram comparison was not conclusive. The owner, or the narration director's sheet for 13_1, should confirm the long o.

Van Loan.note: Charles Van Loan, American. The lookup tool guessed a Dutch reading from the spelling, which was discarded. No written source was found; 'van LOHN', like the English word loan, is the conventional reading. Spoken at 13_1: ask the owner if he knows better.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy
probe.verdict: VERIFIED by transcript: 'Van Lone' heard as Van Lone 3/3 and the plain spelling as Van Lone 2/3 (the third a carrier slip); the decoy 'Van LOO-an' heard as Van Lohan, Van Lowen, Van Luanen. The tool cannot verify a real-word respelling, hence its UNVERIFIED.

Padé.note: Henri Padé, French [pade]. Spoken at 13_5 ('a Padé approximant').

commutator.note: A term of art, spoken at 14_6 and 15_3, 15_4; the risk is a read that drops a syllable and lands on 'commuter'.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy
probe.verdict: VERIFIED by transcript: the plain word heard as 'commutator' 3/3 in every position; the decoy 'commuter' heard as 'commuter' 3/3, so the ASR does tell the two apart (the tool's similarity score called the decoy a match).

communicability.note: Estrada and Hatano's term, spoken once at 11_6; a seven-syllable word the voice may hurry.

eigenvalue.note: Spoken once at 13_5 ('the eigenvalue video'); Video K owns the word.

probe.date: 2026-10-13, michael, ftts 0.1.11, fw 0.10.0, 3 carriers, control + decoy
probe.verdict: PARTIAL: the plain word heard as 'eigenvalue' in the medial and final carriers and as 'Egin value' at a sentence start; the respelling EYE-gen-val-yoo failed (heard as letters). The script says it once, mid-sentence (13_5), so the plain word stands; the narration sheet for 13_5 should be checked.
